about.story.p1.value: I didn't set out to be an agile trainer. I started as a graduate trainee at SSA after a Masters at UMIST, writing code for ERP systems on AS400. What followed was fifteen years at Boehringer Ingelheim - moving from systems analyst to Head of IS Consulting to leading a global SAP deployment across six countries.
about.story.p1.label: Story, first paragraph

about.story.p2.value: It was inside Boehringer that I first got serious about agile - pioneering a Scrum-wrapped-with-DSDM approach to enterprise SAP rollouts at a time when most organisations considered the two incompatible. It worked. Not perfectly, but well enough to prove the point.
about.story.p2.label: Story, second paragraph

about.story.p3.value: In 2016 I went independent, founding Altogether Agile and building a training and coaching practice from the ground up. I've worked as an affiliate trainer with QA, Metadata Training, and TCC; as a Scrum Master and Assessor at the Agile Business Consortium; and as a Visiting Lecturer at the University of Westminster since 2020.
about.story.p3.label: Story, third paragraph

about.story.p4.value: Altogether Agile is now the centre of gravity - training, coaching, knowledge base, and platform in one place. One person, nearly 30 years of experience, and a genuine belief that agile works when it's taught and coached by someone who's actually done it.
about.story.p4.label: Story, fourth paragraph

about.mission.p1.value: Most agile training is too abstract. It describes frameworks without connecting them to real problems. It teaches the events without explaining why they exist. It certifies people who leave the course without knowing what to do on Monday morning.
about.mission.p1.label: Mission, first paragraph

about.mission.p2.value: Altogether Agile exists to close that gap. That means every technique connects to a real decision, not a hypothetical one - and every session ends with something concrete enough to act on.
about.mission.p2.label: Mission, second paragraph
about.mission.p2.hint: The teal mission band. This one is set in bolder white

about.mission.p3.value: Every course, every coaching conversation, and every technique in the knowledge base is designed to be immediately usable - not a concept to be filed away for later. That means real scenarios, honest facilitation, and a trainer who's been in the room for real.
about.mission.p3.label: Mission, third paragraph

about.philosophy.1.body.value: Most agile training fails not because people don't understand the concepts - but because they've never had to apply them under real conditions. Good training puts people in those conditions safely, with a facilitator who's been in the room for real.

about.philosophy.2.body.value: The best coaching conversations don't end with a solution handed over. They end with the person finding their own clarity - which means they own it, and they're more likely to act on it. My job is to ask the right questions, hold the space, and get out of the way.
about.philosophy.2.body.label: Card 2 body
about.philosophy.2.body.hint: The two philosophy cards. The right card

about.philosophy.2.principles.value:
ICF-aligned approach throughout
Experience in the room, but not imposing it
The coachee's agenda, not mine
Honest feedback when it's asked for
